headline: 229 of 450 customers started KYC but got stuck mid-steps
executiveReadout: The clearest observed pattern is not blanket refusal: 229 calls were with customers who had already entered the KYC flow and described specific blockers such as upload stops, OTP confusion, selfie/camera issues, mismatch questions, or weak-network failures. Separately, 109 calls were unreachable or wrong-number outcomes, which points to contact-data and retry-timing issues rather than KYC-step diagnosis. Another 106 calls were short refusals or callback requests, indicating the dialer should distinguish stop-contact requests from reschedulable cases. The immediate operational opportunity is to stop wasting volume on wrong numbers and explicit refusals, while making recovery outreach more step-specific for customers who already attempted KYC.

topInsights.title: Started KYC, then stopped at a specific step
topInsights.readout: 229 calls fell into clusters where customers described an exact failure point after starting KYC: stopped mid-process (70), unclear flow/timing (60), selfie/camera block (46), name/address mismatch (40), and weak-network upload failure (13).
topInsights.whyItMatters: This is the largest lane in the campaign, so generic reminder calling is likely missing what customers actually reported on the call.
topInsights.suggestedChange: Send follow-up that resumes from the failed step and names the likely blocker category: upload, OTP, selfie/camera, mismatch, or network retry.
evidenceQuotes: "last mein kuch document upload pe atak gaya tha"
"mujhe samajh nahi aaya ki Aadhaar wala OTP kis number pe jayega"
"Selfie pe hi atak raha tha, camera permission shayad off tha"
"Current address aur Aadhaar address same nahi tha."

topInsights.title: Unreachable and wrong-number calls consumed 109 of 450 attempts
topInsights.readout: 79 calls had no customer connected and 30 reached the wrong number, totaling 24.2% of all analyzed calls.
topInsights.whyItMatters: These calls do not reveal KYC-step issues and repeated retries to the same number risk wasting volume and repeating mistakes.
topInsights.suggestedChange: Suppress wrong numbers immediately for that customer identity, and move unreachable cases to alternate retry windows and non-voice nudges instead of repeated same-slot calling.
evidenceQuotes: "Nahi, wrong number hai. Yahan Neha nahi hain."
"Yahan koi Pooja nahi hai."
"mujhe aise calls aate rehte hain"

topInsights.title: Explicit stop-calling requests are concentrated and easy to isolate
topInsights.readout: 54 calls were direct refusals, with 53 negative outcomes, and the language was short and unambiguous.
topInsights.whyItMatters: These are poor candidates for continued live outreach and should not be mixed with callback-later or troubleshooting cases.
topInsights.suggestedChange: Apply strong suppression after explicit refusal and remove these numbers from repeated KYC call cycles where policy allows.
evidenceQuotes: "mujhe abhi interest nahi hai"
"Calls mat kariye baar baar."
"Please don't explain anything."

topInsights.title: Callback requests are common but currently mixed with refusals
topInsights.readout: 52 calls were primarily scheduling requests such as after 6 PM, after 7 PM, in 20 minutes, or tomorrow morning.
topInsights.whyItMatters: These customers did not provide a KYC diagnosis on that call; random redials will miss the requested window and create avoidable repeat contacts.
topInsights.suggestedChange: Capture requested callback slots in the dialer and route the follow-up to a short script that starts from the pending KYC step.
evidenceQuotes: "6 baje ke baad call kar lena"
"20 minute baad kar lena"
"main meeting mein hoon abhi"

topInsights.title: Selfie, camera, and image-capture problems account for 46 calls
topInsights.readout: 46 calls specifically mentioned selfie, camera permission, blank screen, or blurred photo issues; these calls were long on average at 195 seconds.
topInsights.whyItMatters: These are concrete product or instruction failures, and long calls suggest agents are spending time troubleshooting steps that could be handled earlier in-app or by message.
topInsights.suggestedChange: Add pre-step camera checks, permission prompts, blur guidance, and resume directly at the selfie/photo step after failure.
evidenceQuotes: "Camera permission ka kuch issue aa raha tha."
"Camera permission diya tha but kuch blank aa raha tha."
"PAN ka photo blur bol raha tha."

topInsights.title: Mismatch confusion is a distinct blocker, not general hesitation
topInsights.readout: 40 calls centered on name or address mismatch questions, often involving PAN name differences or Aadhaar current-versus-old address.
topInsights.whyItMatters: These customers were asking what to submit, not whether to continue, so generic reminders are unlikely to resolve the issue.
topInsights.suggestedChange: Show field-level mismatch guidance before submission, with examples for initials, middle names, and address-proof handling.
evidenceQuotes: "Name mismatch aa raha tha PAN pe."
"Aadhaar mein purana address hai aur current alag hai."
"mujhe complete karna tha but name mismatch jaisa kuch aa raha tha."

topInsights.title: OTP, process length, and step-order confusion appear before hard failures
topInsights.readout: Across the 60 unclear-flow calls and many of the 70 stopped-mid-process calls, customers asked where OTP would arrive, what video KYC meant, how long it would take, and why different channels showed different instructions.
topInsights.whyItMatters: Some drop-off may occur before submission because customers start without knowing requirements, time needed, or where the next step lives.
topInsights.suggestedChange: Test a pre-start checklist covering estimated time, required documents, OTP destination, and whether the next step happens in app, by link, or by video.
evidenceQuotes: "Video KYC jaisa kuch open hua tha"
"mujhe samajh nahi aaya ki Aadhaar wala OTP kis number pe jayega"
"mujhe email pe kuch aaya tha aur app pe kuch aur dikh raha tha."

workflowChanges.title: Suppress wrong numbers at the identity-number pair
workflowChanges.change: Block further KYC calls to that number for the named customer and trigger phone-mapping review on source records.
workflowChanges.measurement: Track repeat wrong-number rate, suppressed-volume share, and any later successful contact via corrected number.

workflowChanges.title: Split callback requests from refusal outcomes in the dialer
workflowChanges.change: Require agents to tag either explicit refusal or customer-requested callback window, with selectable time slots for callback-later cases.
workflowChanges.measurement: Compare contact success and repeat-call count for scheduled callbacks versus unscheduled retries.

workflowChanges.title: Send step-specific recovery messages after partial KYC
workflowChanges.targetMoment: Within hours after a call where the customer described a failed KYC step
workflowChanges.change: Message the exact pending step and tailored help: upload, OTP, selfie/camera, mismatch, or network retry, with a direct resume path.
workflowChanges.measurement: Track resume starts, step completion from the same failed step, and abandonment after recovery outreach.

workflowChanges.title: Add pre-start checklist before upload and video steps
workflowChanges.targetMoment: Before the customer enters KYC or resumes after a reminder
workflowChanges.change: Show estimated completion time, required documents, OTP destination, device requirement for camera steps, and when video KYC appears.
workflowChanges.measurement: Monitor drop-off before first submission step, help-content views, and completion rate by checklist exposure.

workflowChanges.title: Add camera and network readiness checks
workflowChanges.targetMoment: Right before selfie/photo/video capture and upload-heavy steps
workflowChanges.change: Prompt for camera permission, basic image-quality check, and network guidance such as switching to Wi‑Fi if available; preserve progress on failure.
workflowChanges.measurement: Track failure rate at selfie/upload steps, retry success after readiness prompts, and repeat calls mentioning camera or network issues.

openQuestions: Which exact KYC screen or API step failed most often for the 70 stopped-mid-process calls? Current clustering shows symptoms, not product event logs.
How often did customers who asked for a callback actually get called within the requested time window?
For unreachable calls, what retry times, carrier patterns, or geography explain no-answer versus failed-connect outcomes?
How often did customers receive inconsistent instructions across app, email, SMS, and agent script, especially around OTP and video KYC?
For mismatch cases, which document combinations and field mismatches are most common: initials, middle name, old address, or transliteration differences?
What share of selfie/camera failures came from permission denial versus app blank-screen bugs versus image-quality rejection?
Can resume links deep-link to the exact failed step today, or does the customer restart the full flow?
What downstream completion happened after these calls by cluster? The current readout shows call outcomes, not confirmed KYC completion by blocker type.
